Title: Diagnosis
Details: The bug report states that encoding an empty byte array using Base64.encode(new byte[0]) returns CRLF instead of an empty byte array. The test case `testBase64EmptyOutputStream()` passes empty arrays for both encoded and decoded expecting no output on encoding or decoding empty input. The test uses the helper method `testByteByByte()` which performs streaming encode and decode using `Base64OutputStream`. 

The constructor of `Base64OutputStream` initializes a `Base64` instance with the specified line length and separator. The `close()` method of `Base64OutputStream` calls `base64.encode(singleByte, 0, -1)` to notify the encoder of EOF. 

The root cause likely resides within the main encoding method `Base64.encodeBase64(byte[], boolean, boolean)`. This method handles the empty input case on line 683-684 by returning the input array immediately if it is null or empty. However, the encoding path that the `Base64OutputStream` uses appears to notify EOF by encoding with length -1, which could cause the internal buffer to emit a CRLF sequence even for empty input.

This behavior deviates from `Base64.encode(byte[])` which calls `encodeBase64` directly and returns the empty array properly. The `Base64OutputStream` when closed incorrectly triggers output generation (CRLF) for empty input in streaming mode due to EOF signalling in `Base64OutputStream.close()`. This causes the test to fail due to the unexpected CRLF bytes instead of empty output for empty input.

In summary, the bug is caused by the `Base64OutputStream` emitting newline characters (CRLF) on EOF even when encoding an empty array whereas the `Base64` static encode methods return the empty array immediately as expected. The key difference is how EOF notification in streaming encoding triggers unexpected extra output. This matches the symptom reported in the bug report and the failed test case.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
